items.t: U.S. closes loophole that let Chinese companies use top AI chips in foreign data centers
items.d: The Commerce Department further restricted the sale of American AI chips, addressing concerns about how Chinese companies might evade U.S. export restrictions.
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence U.S. closes loophole that let Chinese companies use top AI chips through foreign data centers The Bureau of Industry and Security announced Monday morning that it would clamp down on the sale of chips to data center customers in Southeast Asian countries. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has faced questions in recent months about why the department's Entity List had not been updated for over a year. Alex Brandon / AP Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 16, 2026, 1:44 PM EST By Jared Perlo The Commerce Department moved to further restrict the sale of top-tier American AI chips Monday morning, addressing mounting concerns about how companies in China and other countries might evade American export restrictions by taking advantage of longstanding loopholes. As part of a new rule, data center customers in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil must now receive a special license from the Commerce Department in order to buy advanced AI chips from American companies such as Nvidia or AMD. Over the past several years, businesses in those countries have bought billions of dollars worth’ of high-end chips, raising concerns that some chips might be illegally smuggled into China. The rule, issued by the department’s Bureau of Industry and Security, will also require existing overseas data center customers to receive a similar license if they provide “significant volumes” of computing power to companies whose headquarters are in China, Russia, Cuba or other countries banned from receiving certain types of advanced American technology. Companies in these countries have allowed Chinese businesses to access their most advanced AI chips remotely , skirting rules that prevented Chinese companies from accessing these chips on Chinese territory. items.fullText: Lambda Boosts AI Factory Resiliency and Efficiency With NVIDIA Photonics November 16, 2026 by Brian Sparks 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! To train an AI model, thousands of GPUs have to work together, requiring a network that’s fast, efficient and resilient. Lambda is tackling the network piece of the puzzle with NVIDIA Photonics co-packaged optics (CPO) switches. The cloud provider is using the switches to connect NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks with more than 10,000 GPUs, delivering lower power, higher resiliency and longer mean time between interruptions (MTBI) to an AI factory at scale. “Networking has to keep pace with the demands of increasingly large AI clusters,” said Dave Ward, president of cloud services at Lambda. “Bringing co-packaged optics into a deployment of this scale is an important step toward building the infrastructure needed to support the next generation of AI.” Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 In the company’s tests using the switches, network latency — the time needed for moving data — dropped by about 4% at rack scale and by up to about 10% at pod scale. Across rack, scalable unit and pod configurations, the network maintains the same throughput as conventional pluggable optics. Delivering Power Efficiency and Resiliency at Scale Improving power efficiency and resiliency matters because the network sits at the center of AI factory productivity. In a large training job, one interrupted link can stall thousands of GPUs. With agentic inference, one network disruption can introduce cascading latency effects on many agents. Every interruption costs time, and every watt spent on networking is a watt not available for compute. NVIDIA Photonics addresses both power efficiency and resiliency. By replacing pluggable transceivers with co-packaged optical engines on the switch package, it delivers up to 5x better power efficiency and up to 15x higher reliability than conventional pluggable optics. items.fullText: CUDA at 20: How the Platform Transformed Scientific Computing Over two decades, CUDA, the platform that turned GPUs into the engine of modern science, has advanced Nobel Prize-winning research and more. November 16, 2026 by Brett Murray 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! This week at SC26, NVIDIA is marking two decades of CUDA by honoring the researchers, developers and engineers who helped make GPU computing a foundation for modern science and AI. CUDA’s 20th anniversary presents an occasion to reflect across computing eras, from the people who wrote the very first CUDA programs to the AI developers building on their work today. At the platform’s core is this developer community whose experiments, tools and persistence expanded what accelerated computing could do. From SC06 to SC26 NVIDIA announced CUDA in November 2006 and brought it to the scientific community at SC06, giving scientists and developers a familiar, high-level programming model for using GPUs. It fundamentally extended accelerated computing beyond graphics use cases to accelerate demanding applications for science, simulation and more. In the two decades since, developers have used CUDA to advance Nobel Prize-winning AI research , accelerate scientific applications on supercomputers and support visual effects in Oscar-winning films . Today, more than 11 million developers build on CUDA across the computing stack. items.fullText: NVIDIA Announces Rubin HPC — A New GPU to Accelerate Agents for Science, Engineering and Analytics A record leap in CUDA cores with accelerated data movement shorten time to results for science and engineering workloads. November 16, 2026 by Dan Ernst 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Announced today at SC26, NVIDIA Rubin HPC is a new GPU in the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform designed to accelerate simulation and data processing for science, engineering and analytics workflows. As agents help scientists and engineers explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs, they rely on simulations to test those ideas and guide their next steps. Rubin HPC will accelerate those simulations, shortening the path from exploration to scientific discovery and industrial design. The Rubin HPC GPU features a record number of CUDA cores — more than 50,000 on a single GPU — as well as a sparse data acceleration capability that keeps those cores fed with data, and accelerates GPU-to-GPU connectivity with seventh-generation NVIDIA NVLink interconnect technology. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Scientists and engineers rely on simulation to understand complex systems before committing to experiments or physical prototypes. Working with agents, these teams can explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs. This increases demand for the GPU-accelerated simulations needed to evaluate those ideas and guide next steps. “For agents tackling science and engineering, faster simulation means faster discovery,” said Ian Buck , vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. “Rubin HPC accelerates the simulations agents use to test ideas and guide their next steps, helping scientists and engineers explore more possibilities and bring breakthroughs closer.” Turning Faster Computation Into Faster Discovery Across climate models, engineering simulations, genomic analysis and financial risk, scientific computing w

items.t: US tightens AI chip export controls to deter Chinese companies from accessing compute remotely
items.d: Under the interim rule, the U.S. will require firms to get licenses to export AI chips if they may provide compute to China or other restricted countries.
items.fullText: The Trump administration on Monday is preparing to roll out new export controls on AI chips and data centers outside the U.S., seeking to prevent companies, especially those in China, from getting past U.S. export controls by remotely accessing AI infrastructure located in other countries. Under the interim rule , the Commerce Department will require companies to get licenses to export, reexport, or transfer AI chips and servers to data centers anywhere in the world if they may provide compute to companies in China or other restricted countries. The remote-access rules target companies based in the U.S.’s D:5 group of embargoed countries, which includes China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, and 18 others. The U.S. already has rules requiring chip companies to get a license to ship AI chips to companies based in, or owned by any business in, this group of countries. “This new control is a logical extension of existing controls,” the interim rule reads. “These restrictions will undermine the ability of companies headquartered in countries of concern from using U.S. advanced Super Intelligence (SI) semiconductors to train advanced SI models.” The move comes days after Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned amid a scandal involving an alleged Chinese spy linked to one of the chipmaker’s customers. The U.S. government has reportedly been wanting to put that customer, Megaspeed, on a special entity list, as it believes the company has been buying thousands of Nvidia chips to provide compute to Chinese businesses to get past existing export-control restrictions. Reuters reported last week that Chinese AI companies are rushing to secure computing capacity overseas amid fears of tighter restrictions from the U.S. The rule applies to data centers or any network that can supply over 12 million total processing performance (TPP), an export-control metric the U.S. uses to measure computing power. items.fullText: NVIDIA Announces New Planned Investments in Korean Startups at the MSIT-NVIDIA AI Startup Partnership Forum November 9, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT and NVIDIA hosted the MSIT -NVIDIA AI Startup Partnership Forum at COEX. Representatives from the Ministry of Science and ICT and NVIDIA met with over 20 Korean startups across foundation models, physical AI, AI infrastructure and AI semiconductors. NVIDIA also announced an investment in Korean startup Point2 , with additional investments planned in Motif Technologies , RLWRLD and Upstage. Point2 Technology, an AI interconnect company, builds scalable, radio frequency-based interconnects that move data between chips and racks in AI factories, offering an innovative alternative to conventional copper and optical interconnect solutions for AI cluster scale-up, delivering the reach, performance and efficiency needed for next-generation AI infrastructure. Motif Technologies , a Seoul-based AI lab, develops foundation models for building AI agents that carry out complex tasks, including Motif-3, a large language model released with open weights. RLWRLD, a physical AI startup based in San Francisco, Seoul and Tokyo, develops robotics foundation models that enable humanoid and industrial robots to perform complex real-world tasks that require five-finger dexterity, such as precisely inserting components, threading nuts onto bolts and kitting parts from moving conveyors. Upstage , a Korean enterprise AI company, develops Solar language models and document AI tools that help businesses extract information from complex documents, streamline workflows and build AI applications for everyday operations. The companies represent work across the full AI stack , from infrastructure to models to robotics applications. items.fullText: From Chips to Skills, NVIDIA and Korea Expand Sovereign AI Collaboration November 8, 2026 by Jesse Clayton 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA and Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT) are expanding their collaboration across the country’s sovereign AI ecosystem, from AI semiconductors and data center infrastructure to talent, startups, models, agents and security. The collaboration lays the groundwork for Korean NPU and XPU companies to explore participation in the NVIDIA NVLink Fusion ecosystem, and includes NVIDIA training and certification programs, hackathons and technical seminars to strengthen GPU utilization. Through Korea’s AI for All initiative, NVIDIA will collaborate with three selected consortia and four leading Korean foundation model builders, using NVIDIA Dynamo software to optimize and scale AI inference. In addition, NVIDIA today announced a collaboration with SK Telecom and Rebellions, supported by MSIT, to advance sovereign AI infrastructure for Korean models and workloads with NVIDIA NVLink Fusion. items.t: 반도체 ‘호황 지도’…엔비디아 쏠림 줄고 중국 비중 커졌다
items.fullText: 본문 경제 산업·재계 반도체 ‘호황 지도’…엔비디아 쏠림 줄고 중국 비중 커졌다 배지현 기자 수정 2026-11-17 02:18 펼침 0:00 Your browser does not support the audio element. 삼성전자·SK하이닉스 분기보고서 삼성전자와 에스케이(SK)하이닉스. 연합뉴스 광고 메모리 초호황 속에 삼성전자와 에스케이(SK)하이닉스의 ‘고객 지도’가 달라지고 있다. 하이닉스는 엔비디아로 추정되는 최대 고객에 대한 의존도가 낮아졌고, 삼성전자는 자체 인공지능 칩을 만드는 아마존 등이 주요 고객으로 자리잡았다. 미국 주도의 공급망 재편 속에서도 두 회사의 중국 매출 비중이 나란히 늘어난 것으로 나타났다. 16일 공시된 삼성전자·에스케이하이닉스의 분기보고서를 보면, 하이닉스의 올해 1∼9월 매출 236조5105억원 가운데 매출의 10% 이상을 차지한 고객은 두 곳이다. 엔비디아로 추정되는 고객 ‘가’의 매출이 34조9778억원(14.8%), 고객 ‘나’가 23조8509억원(10.1%)이다. 지난해 같은 기간엔 엔비디아 추정 고객의 매출 비중이 27%(17조3551억원)를 차지했다. 엔비디아 매출이 두 배로 늘었지만, 비중은 절반 가까이 줄어든 셈이다. 업계에선 고객 ‘나’도 마이크로소프트나 구글 등 빅테크(거대기술 기업) 중 한 곳으로 추정한다. 삼성전자가 공개한 올해 1∼9월 주요 매출처는 구글 모회사 알파벳·아마존·애플·홍콩 테크트로닉스·수프림일렉트로닉스로, 이들 다섯 곳이 전체 매출의 약 24%를 차지했다. 인공지능 반도체 시장을 이끈 엔비디아는 없지만, 텐서처리장치(TPU)와 트레이니엄 등 자체 개발 칩을 만들고 데이터센터를 확장하고 있는 구글과 아마존이 이름을 올렸다. 광고 중국 비중은 두 회사 모두 커졌다. 하이닉스의 올해 1∼9월 연결 기준 중국 매출은 56조1378억원으로 전체의 23.7%를 차지했다. 지난해 같은 기간(18.3%)보다 5%포인트 넘게 늘었다. 반면 미국 매출 비중은 전년 동기 70.2%였지만 올해 62.5%로 낮아졌다. 삼성전자도 해외 판매법인까지 합친 연결 기준 중국 매출이 114조5562억원으로, 지난해 같은 기간(31조7990억원)의 3.6배 가량 늘었다. 매출 비중 기준 13.3%에서 22.9%로 뛰었다. 연결 기준 최대 시장은 여전히 미주(243조9316억원)지만, 삼성전자 본사의 수출 매출만 보는 별도 기준으로는, 중국이 미주를 앞서면서 2024년 이후 3년째 선두를 지켰다. 삼성전자 5대 매출처에 이름을 올린 홍콩 테크트로닉스와 수프림일렉트로닉스는 각각 홍콩과 대만에 기반을 둔 반도체 유통기업으로, 중화권에 공급되는 반도체를 상당 부분 맡는 것으로 알려졌다. 두 회사의 호황은 메모리값 급등에 기대고 있다. 삼성전자의 올해 1∼9월 매출은 500조6261억원으로 전년 동기 대비 108.8% 증가했다. 실적 성장은 반도체 사업이 주도했는데 반도체를 담당하는 디바이스솔루션(DS) 부문의 누적 매출만 356조3358억원이었다. 메모리 반도체 평균 판매가격이 지난해 평균보다 약 270% 올랐고, 디(D)램 시장점유율도 회사 추정 기준 올해 3분기 38.3%로 지난해보다 4.3%포인트 늘었다. 하이닉스도 6세대 고대역폭메모리(HBM4) 판매 비중 확대와 서버용 5세대 디램(DDR5) 판매 증가가 컸다. 3분기 디램 평균판매가격(ASP)은 전 분기보다 20% 후반, 낸드는 20% 중반 상승했다. 회사 쪽이 ‘완판’이라 밝힌만큼 생산설비 가동률은 100%를 유지했다. 광고 광고 한편 완제품도 함께 생산하는 삼성전자에겐 반도체 호황의 그늘도 짙었다. 1∼9월 반도체 부문 영업이익은 249조3958억원으로 전사 영업이익의 98.1%를 차지했으나 스마트폰·가전을 담당하는 디바이스경험(DX) 부문 영업이익은 1조3237억원에 그쳤다. 지난해 연간 영업이익의 10% 남짓 수준이다. 올해 3분기 삼성전자의 글로벌 스마트폰 점유율은 22.1%로 지난해(19.2%)보다 높아졌지만, 치솟은 부품값에 영업이익은 오히려
